results.question: Can my dad use the golf course? He's a retired Marine.
results.answer:
Yes. The Medal of Honor Golf Course is open to retired military, and it's also open to the general public. Retirees get a booking advantage: retired military, veterans and DoD can book tee times up to eight days in advance. That's one day ahead of the general public's seven days. Active-duty members get ten days.

He'll need to bring ID. His first online registration defaults to the General Public category, so he should show it at the Pro Shop to be moved to the retiree category. Dress code is collared shirts and Bermuda-length shorts or skirts.

Want the hours for this time of year? Details: [Golf Course](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/recreation-fitness/recreation/outdoor-recreation/golf-course)

results.question: How do I get my 2-year-old on the waitlist for the child development center?
results.answer:
Start by creating an account at MilitaryChildCare.com. Sign in, finish your household profile, and request care at Quantico. If no space is open, your child goes on the waitlist and you get an offer by email when a spot opens.

The Child Development Centers take children from 6 weeks to 5 years, so a 2-year-old qualifies. Fees are based on total family income. Once you have an offer, you'll complete the registration forms and attend a parent orientation before your child starts.

Want the steps for what to do after you get an offer? Details: [Child Development Centers](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/child-development-centers). You can also call CDC North at 703-784-4470 or CDC South at 703-784-3652 with questions.

Both Child Development Centers, for ages 6 weeks to 5 years, are open Monday to Friday, 6:00am to 6:00pm (as of the saved page, Oct 26, 2026). CDC North is at 703-784-4470 and CDC South is at 703-784-3652. They can tell you your fee and the current wait. The Resource and Referral office at CDC South can also help: 703-784-0674/4453.

results.question: Is there before and after school care for my 8 year old?
results.answer:
Yes. School Age Care (SAC) covers children ages 5-12 in kindergarten through 6th grade. Your 8-year-old fits, and the program includes before and after school care, plus full days on school breaks. Breakfast and an afternoon snack are provided on school days.

The SAC center is at 3312 Purvis Rd and is open Monday-Friday, 6:00am-6:00pm (as of the saved page, Oct 26, 2026). Call 703-784-2249.

To get started, register at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/). If there's no opening, your child goes on a waitlist and you'll be notified when a spot opens. Space is prioritized under DoD rules, so register early.

Are you active duty, a DoD civilian, or another category? I can check whether the priority rules affect you. Details: [School Age Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care)

results.question: I'm trying to figure out if I'm eligible for tuition assistance, and I need to get my Joint Services Transcript — can you help?
results.answer:
Tuition Assistance (TA) is a benefit for **active-duty service members**. Per the Voluntary Education page, DoD civilians and family members can't submit TA applications. If you're active duty, TA covers up to $4,500 per fiscal year.

For your Joint Services Transcript, you request it online at [jst.doded.mil](https://jst.doded.mil/jst/). That site is outside MCCS. You'll send the JST to your school and upload it to your TA portal. The Voluntary Education Center (703-784-2375) can confirm the steps.

Are you active duty? If so, I can walk you through the TA steps.

Details: [Voluntary Education](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/education)

results.question: My husband is active duty. Can I use tuition assistance for my college classes?
results.answer:
No, military Tuition Assistance (TA) is for active-duty service members only. The Voluntary Education page says DoD civilians and family members are not able to submit TA applications. Your husband can't use it for your classes either.

As a spouse, you may qualify for the My Career Advancement Account (MyCAA) scholarship. It's for spouses of active-duty members in certain pay grades (E-1 to E-9, W-1 to W-2, O-1 to O-3). Spouses of Guard and Reserve members in those same grades are also eligible. The Education Center also supports spouses with FAFSA and other education resources.

Want his pay grade checked against the MyCAA eligibility, or the Education Center's contact info so you can set up an advising appointment?

Details: [Voluntary Education](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/voluntary-education)

results.question: We're PCSing to Quantico next month with two kids and a dog. Where can we stay while we look for housing?
results.answer:
The best fit is probably **Inns of the Corps Quantico**. It's the on-base hotel that takes PCS families, and it has a limited number of pet-friendly rooms. Call early to ask about pet rooms and space for four. PCS families can book up to one year ahead. Reservations: 703-630-4444 or the 24/7 line at 888-409-7829. Details are as of the page's saved date (Oct 26, 2026).

Two things to know:
- The Inns has 42 efficiencies and 24 suites, which are worth asking about with two kids.
- Credentials are required at check-in, so bring your orders and ID.

Are you the active-duty Marine, or the spouse? That affects which options you'll want me to walk through next.

results.question: How do I book a room at the Inns of the Corps?
results.answer:
You can book by calling the 24/7 reservation line at **1-888-409-7829**, or by phoning the Inns directly at 703-630-4444. A valid credit or debit card is required at check-in.

How far ahead you can book depends on your trip:
- **PCS families:** up to one year ahead
- **TAD/TDY:** 90 days ahead
- **Leisure stays:** 30 days ahead

Valid credentials are required at check-in. Eligible guests include active duty, Guard, Reserve, retirees on leave or official duty, DoD civilians, FBI/DEA, and OCS students with orders. For group bookings, email LodgingReservations.Quantico@usmc-mccs.org.

results.question: My husband deployed two months ago and I'm really overwhelmed and not sleeping. Is there someone I can talk to?
results.answer:
I'm sorry you're carrying so much right now. Two months into a deployment, with little sleep, is hard, and reaching out is a good step.

The quickest option is **Semper Support**. It's free, confidential, non-medical counseling for Marine families, and you don't need an appointment. Call 800-342-9647. Eligible spouses can get up to 12 sessions per issue.

If you'd rather talk in person, the **Community Counseling Program** at Little Hall, Suite 200, takes spouses and families. Call 703-784-2570 to set up a visit. Hours as of the page's saved date (Oct 26, 2026): Mon, Wed, Thu, and Fri 7:30am–4:30pm, and Tue 7:30am–7:00pm.

If things ever feel like too much or you have thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text **988, then press 1**, any time. For an emergency, call 911.

Want me to share the details for the New Parent Support or Marine Corps Family Team Building deployment programs too?

Details: [Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling), [Semper Support](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/semper-support)

results.question: I get out next year. How do I sign up for SkillBridge?
results.answer:
Congrats on getting close to your EAS. At Quantico, you start by attending the **SkillBridge Information Session**. It's required before you can submit any paperwork. Registration is required (no walk-ins) and closes 2 days before the session. The next one is Tuesday, Oct 27, so it's likely closed. After that: Nov 10, Dec 1, and Dec 15, all 1:00-3:00 PM (dates as of the saved page, Oct 26, 2026).

Steps:
1. Attend the info session (register on Eventbrite).
2. Confirm eligibility. You need 180+ days of active duty, and the Transition Readiness Seminar done at least 180 days before separation.
3. Get your command's approval. SkillBridge is at the commander's discretion.
4. Research DoD-approved SkillBridge partners and get an acceptance letter.
5. Submit your packet to the installation SkillBridge office, then route it through MyMarineEducation for final command authorization.

Timing depends on your rank. You can start up to 120 days before separation (E1-E5) or up to 90 days (E6 and above). Tell me your rank group and I can say who approves it.

Details: [SkillBridge](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/transition-readiness-program/skillbridge). Questions go to Transition Readiness at 703-784-4963.
